summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with right-sided testicular pain and swelling, presenting with fever and leukocytosis. He was diagnosed with febrile epididymo-orchitis, supported by scrotal ultrasound showing right testicular inflammation and a complex hydrocele likely representing a pyocele. He was treated with IV cefepime initially, with improvement in symptoms and white blood cell count. Urine cultures grew E. coli resistant to ciprofloxacin and Bactrim, and pan-sensitive Proteus, both sensitive to cephalosporins. He remained afebrile, and his renal function and potassium normalized. He was discharged on oral cefpodoxime for a 14-day course, with updated warfarin dosing and instructions to follow up with his urologist and primary care provider. His chronic conditions, including heart failure, diabetes, cirrhosis, and anticoagulation, were managed without complication.
